transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, my name is Hayley. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah hi Hayley, um, I got your new Hub 5 installed on Tuesday afternoon by the Openreach contractor, and ever since then, you know, our Wi-Fi upstairs is completely dead across all four bedrooms.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can look into your router hardware record today. Before I check the device details, please provide your installation address and security PIN.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Address is 53 Victoria Crescent, um, Glasgow, G12 9DE, and the security PIN is three nine zero eight.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that confirms the account details for your Gigabit Full Fibre contract. What seems to be happening with the signal in the upstairs rooms?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Our Wi-Fi is dead upstairs. We can't get any connection in the study or the bedrooms.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your Wi-Fi is dead upstairs, okay. That is typically related to structural attenuation and high frequency absorption in residential properties.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Our old Hub 3 worked all over the house for five years without any dead zones, um, but this new Hub 5 won't even reach the first floor landing, let alone the back study!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Hub 5 broadcasts higher frequency Wi-Fi 6 spectrum on eighty megahertz wide channels, which attenuates much more rapidly through dense brickwork and masonry.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am paying fifty-five pounds a month for Gigabit speeds, and I can't even open a work email on my laptop upstairs! I lost half a day's consulting billable hours yesterday because the connection kept dropping! It is completely infuriating!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wireless speeds and indoor radio propagation are never guaranteed within customer premises under the residential terms of service.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am not asking for gigabit speeds in the attic, I am asking for a basic stable connection that doesn't drop dead every five minutes while I'm on work calls!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Where is the router physically placed in the ground floor hallway, and are there any metal mirrors or electronic appliances nearby?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's on a wooden side table in the hall, um, right by the front door where the Openreach engineer mounted the optical wall box next to the radiator.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A large metal radiator adjacent to the router acts as a massive reflector, deflecting electromagnetic radio waves away from the ceiling and staircase.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Our walls are solid Victorian sandstone, like eighteen inches thick with lathe and plaster ceilings. But like I said, the old hub had zero issues reaching upstairs.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Older hubs utilized wider legacy 2.4GHz channels that penetrated thick masonry at the expense of overall gigabit throughput speed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can we not just turn on that 2.4GHz mode on this new hub then, or separate the frequencies like people suggest online?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Hub 5 firmware manages band steering automatically across both bands using centralized cloud algorithms without manual frequency splitting.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you check if there is a pending firmware patch for it on your network, or if this specific unit has a defective internal antenna array?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Hang on a second while I pull up the equipment dispatch log.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, I can see the serial number of the hub dispatched on Monday morning.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, and does your remote diagnostic test show anything physically wrong with the Wi-Fi antennas or radio chips inside it?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The remote diagnostic shows the hub optical interface is receiving nine hundred and forty megabits down.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, but what about the wireless transmitters? Are the antennas functioning at full power?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our remote portal does not provide individual component RF power telemetry for internal router antennas.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well what are we supposed to do then? We can't work from the hallway sofa all day.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You would need to purchase third-party gigabit powerline network adapters or a dedicated tri-band mesh Wi-Fi system from an independent electronics retailer.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why should I spend eighty to a hundred pounds on third-party mesh extenders when S-Net advertises reliable whole home broadband on television?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Whole Home Wi-Fi guarantee is an optional subscription add-on priced at eight pounds extra per calendar month on top of your existing package.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You're joking! Another eight pounds a month just to get the service I'm already paying fifty-five pounds for every four weeks?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That add-on includes up to three S-Net Intelligent Wi-Fi mesh discs with guaranteed thirty megabit throughput coverage in every habitable room.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you not send me one complimentary booster disc considering this new hub downgrade was forced on us during the contract renewal?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Standard technical support tier one advisors do not possess administrative authorization to dispatch complimentary booster hardware without the subscription bolt-on code.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can I put the old Hub 3 back on the line instead? I still have it in the cupboard under the stairs in its original packaging.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Hub 3 does not support the optical GPON authentication protocol required for Gigabit Full Fibre street cabinet connections.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So I'm stuck with a shiny new hub that doesn't transmit signal to where I actually need to work.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You could try repositioning the hub off the low wooden table and onto a higher wall mounted shelf to establish a clearer direct line of sight to the open stairwell.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The yellow optical patch cord from the wall termination box is only one metre long, um, so it won't stretch to a high shelf without pulling tight.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Longer SC-APC optical patch cables measuring three or five metres can be purchased online from third-party telecoms accessories suppliers if required.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Always third-party suppliers, isn't it? S-Net takes the money and passes the buck.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We provide standard equipment suitable for standard modern residential construction.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Hold on.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, the system refreshed the customer portal record.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Has that done anything to the Wi-Fi signal?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, that was simply an administrative record sync on our customer relationship database.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right. So basically there is nothing you can do about our dead zone upstairs today without charging me more money.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Unless you wish to add the Whole Home Wi-Fi booster package to your monthly account ledger, there are no further remote radio profiles to adjust.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, I am certainly not paying S-Net a single penny more for a problem your new hub created on Tuesday morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will log ticket reference WF-70192 detailing your reported Wi-Fi attenuation due to Victorian sandstone building construction.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And the signal upstairs is still dead, so nothing is resolved. I'm going to look into cancelling under the fourteen-day cooling off period.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The customer cancellations department can explain contract termination terms and cooling off clauses if you call during weekday business hours.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will be calling them first thing tomorrow morning, you can count on that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else I can assist with regarding your broadband connection today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, nothing.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net as your broadband provider. Have a good afternoon, goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Bye.
